item.title: Here's how much it would cost Michigan to fire Kyle Whittingham
item.description: A disastrous Michigan football season has the fans raising their metaphorical pitch forks. It hit a new low this weekend, when the Wolverines were punked 15-6 in their own house by a Michigan State team that hadn't won a football game in nearly two months and was down half of its original starting roster. With an offense stuck in reverse and a special teams unit that is seemingly incapable of making kicks, much less big plays, the bulk of the problems seems to lie on the coaching staff. The Free Press wrote earlier this fall about offensive coordinator Jason Beck's buyout , but it's legitimate to wonder if he may not be the only coach on the hot seat. Head coach Kyle Whittingham seems in over his head in Ann Arbor, and the question becomes: Does a new athletic director allow him another season to try and implement his culture and scheme, or will they simply cut bait and start anew? MICHIGAN GRADES: MSU debacle a failure on all accounts Whittingham, who turns 67 on Nov. 21, signed a five-year deal last offseason worth $41 million, according to his contract obtained by the Free Press. Per that contract, if U-M relieves him of duties at any point during that window, he is owed an "amount equivalent to 75% of the Head Coach's Base Salary in monthly installments for the remainder of the scheduled Term of this Agreement." He's set to be paid $33.0 million over the next four years, which would mean a buyout would cost $24.75 million. The deal says he's required to seek immediate employment, but it's more likely this would be a retirement given his age and where he's at in his career; it's unclear how that would affect the buyout, if at all. The $25 million is a drop in the bucket in the grand scheme of U-M spending, but it would be the department's latest eight-figure amount that goes toward something off the field. Michigan is still finishing payments of more than $30 million in NCAA fines for sign stealing, recently paid more than $12 million to a law firm for an internal review of its athletic department culture, and is soon to pay more than $7 million to buy out athletic director Warde Manuel, scheduled for next month. U-M has hired president C. Cybele Raver to oversee the university and hired search firm ZRG Turnkey to assist with finding its next athletic director. U-M will not only hire an AD but a Chief Revenue Officer for the department, who will handle the financial decisions. The two are required to work hand-in-hand moving forward, a person with knowledge of the search told the Detroit Free Press. The money is not a good enough reason to keep Whittingham around, but timing could be difficult unless an AD is hired and onboarded sometime in the next 45 days. U-M was on the back end of the cycle when it hired Whittingham late last December, and while he was able to get his staff in place and a transfer portal class on board, that hasn't yielded results. The coaching carousel will pick up in earnest the week after Thanksgiving, which is 21 days

item.title: Karl-Anthony Towns hits back at people who disregard the importance of rebounding
item.description: Karl-Anthony Towns hits back at people who disregard the importance of rebounding originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Karl-Anthony Towns is one of the league's best rebounders, and despite how important rebounds are, it seems to be disrespected. Towns has been quite an impactful player on the boards for a long time, which was evident during the New York Knicks ' championship run in 2026. Since then, Towns has kept being a nuisance on the boards. He is averaging 13.6 rebounds per game this season to go along with his 20.9 points a night. Towns is second in the league in rebounds, only behind Sacramento Kings center Domantas Sabonis, who is averaging 14.6 rebounds per game. Karl-Anthony Towns defends the value of rebounding in the NBA Most older basketball fans and players would agree that rebounding is a necessary skill for teams to have in the league. These days, the other stats tend to get a lot of love, especially points, assists, steals, and blocks. However, Towns has come to rebounding's defense because they are probably even more important now. With the abundance of three-pointers being taken, maximizing the number of possessions with rebounds means more opportunities to score points. MORE: Karl-Anthony Towns has gotten honest about how he can be impactful during his off nights A notion that has popped up recently is that the rebounds are not as "sexy" as the other statistics. That is something that Towns certainly disagrees with. "It's a sexy stat to me that damn sure looks sexy to me. Rebounding to me is about establishing the confidence of this team to shoot the ball with full confidence and allowing them to understand that, regardless of the result," Towns said after the Knicks' impressive win on Saturday . "If you take care of the process and do your best with your jumper or your finishing, your teammate has your back." Moving forward, more people should appreciate the value of rebounding. Sometimes, it could be the difference between a team winning a championship or being bounced out earlier in the Playoffs. Towns would know because he just won the championship as one of the league's premier rebounders. item.title: Jemimah Rodrigues to lead Mumbai in Super League stage of Senior Women's T20 Trophy
item.description: MUMBAI : India women's team batter Jemimah Rodrigues will lead Mumbai in the upcoming Super League stage of the Senior Women's T20 Trophy. The Super League will be played in Ahmedabad from November 14. Rodrigues had smashed 107 off just 47 balls against Pondicherry in their sixth and last match of the league stage of the Senior Women's T20 in Pune on Friday to star in Mumbai's 83-run victory. Rodrigues' century took Mumbai to the Super League stage of the tournament. Returning from a four-month layoff from the game due to a hamstring injury, Rodrigues had scored 58 off 41 balls against Delhi and 26 not out off 19 balls against Uttar Pradesh in a nine-over game. "Jemi's century yesterday was quite good, because the ball wasn't coming nicely on the bat. There was low bounce, it wasn't a flat pitch, but she placed the ball well, piercing the gap between two fielders, instead of trying to hit the ball hard. She played very smartly; it was a smartly built innings, as, realising the nature of the wicket, she didn't want to go for big shots. She came to bat in the fifth over of the innings and started off with two paddle sweeps, which got her two twos, and then gave us the necessary momentum. She paced her knock well and got to her century in the last over," Mumbai Women's team head coach Ajay Kadam told TOI. Interestingly, despite being the Delhi Capitals captain, Rodrigues wasn't the Mumbai skipper in the league stage of the tournament, as she joined the team late. Mumbai were captained by Manali Dakshini. "Jemimah was fine with that. She has no issues with that. She's a team player," Kadam said. Praising the impact of Rodrigues on the team, Kadam said, "Jemimah has definitely added a lot of energy to our dressing room. She has gained vast experience by now. Her presence matters a lot. The girls look up to her. She joined the team after a few matches, but since then, has played her role very well. She has lifted the team to a whole new level, given them confidence. She is a star."

item.title: 🚨 After 30 years! German second-tier club changes its name
item.description: 🚨 After 30 years! German second-tier club changes its name After around three decades, the historic Franconian club is returning to its roots: From the 2027/28 season, SpVgg Greuther Fürth will once again compete as **SpVgg Fürth** and will use the classic circular logo featuring the cloverleaf across the board. The three-time German champions (1914, 1926 and 1929) had included “Greuther” in their name since 1996, when TSV Vestenbergsgreuth’s football division joined the club. What was intended at the time to symbolize the merger of two clubs increasingly came to be seen by many supporters over the years as little more than a relic on paper, with barely any relevance to everyday club life. The return to the club’s roots marks the success of an eight-year campaign: The fan alliance “Back to SpVgg Fürth” secured a decisive milestone at Sunday’s extraordinary general meeting. Of the 2,103 members eligible to vote, 88.3 percent backed the motion, comfortably exceeding the required three-quarters majority. Emotions ran high as opposing views clashed at the meeting. In his speech, honorary president Helmut Hack made an impassioned appeal to retain the name associated with his life’s work. The 77-year-old stressed that he respected the desire for a sense of belonging, but argued that the additional name had not diminished that sense of belonging—it had broadened it. At stake, he said, were the fundamental questions of who they were and who they wanted to be. Representatives of the fan initiative countered that the move was intended to strengthen supporters’ connection to the club and mark a united fresh start. They argued that returning to the club’s roots was in no way a rejection of its history, but rather the foundation for a renewed sense of identity. item.title: Tee Higgins makes his 50th career touchdown catch
item.description: Cincinnati Bengals receiver Tee Higgins recorded his 50th career touchdown catch during the second quarter of an NFL Week 9 game against the Atlanta Falcons at Bernabéu Stadium in Madrid, Spain. Higgins scored on a 4-yard pass from quarterback Joe Burrow . Higgins' 50th career TD reception was his fifth of this season. He's in his seventh NFL season, all with the Bengals. "It's just not fair," NFL Network analyst Louis Riddick said during the broadcast. "It's just not fair. Watch how Tee Higgins catches this ball." Higgins entered the game ranked second in the NFL in receiving yardage this season, trailing only the Seattle Seahawks ' Jaxon Smith-Njigba. Higgins was named AFC Offensive Player of the Week for his effort in Cincinnati's 43-36 overtime win in NFL Week 8 against Tennessee. It was Higgins' first-ever AFC Offensive Player of the Week award. Higgins had 10 catches for 155 receiving yards against the Titans, and caught two of quarterback Joe Burrow's five touchdown passes . After being held without a catch during the first half, Higgins went off during the second half of a Week 7 rout in Baltimore, catching six Joe Burrow passes for 148 receiving yards with a touchdown. Earlier in the second half, Higgins' shoulder and arm were evaluated by medical personnel after he absorbed a big hit from Ravens defensive back Kyle Hamilton after a catch. Before the bye week, Higgins was dealing with an adductor injury he suffered in a Week 4 loss to Jacksonville. item.title: Nagelsmann or Howe? Manchester United hierarchy split over next manager as Michael Carrick's future hangs in the balance
item.description: Manchester United find themselves at a critical crossroads as the club's leadership remains divided over who should lead the team forward. While Michael Carrick remains in the dugout for now, the threat of relegation has sparked intense internal debate regarding a potential high-profile replacement. Internal divide over potential successors The corridors of power at Old Trafford are currently home to a significant difference of opinion regarding the club's long-term managerial direction. As results continue to falter domestically, Manchester United's director of recruitment Christopher Vivell is understood to be championing the appointment of Julian Nagelsmann. The former Bayern Munich and Germany head coach is seen by some as the elite tactical mind capable of modernising the squad. However, technical director Jason Wilcox is reportedly leaning towards a different profile, preferring the Premier League experience of former Newcastle United boss Eddie Howe, as noted by SportBible . This split at the top comes at a time when other major candidates appear to be off the table. Antonio Conte has publicly distanced himself from a return to the dugout following his departure from Napoli, while former England manager Gareth Southgate has indicated he is not looking for an immediate return to coaching. No clear alternative for Carrick Despite the growing noise surrounding his position, there is a sense that the United hierarchy is hesitant to pull the trigger without a concrete plan in place. Famed journalist David Ornstein has provided a sobering update on the situation , suggesting that the board’s lack of action thus far indicates a desire for the current regime to turn things around. "I think the truth here at Old Trafford is that they do want Carrick to succeed," he stated on USA Network. "If they wanted to remove him and make a change I think they'd have already done it by now and found an interim solution." The situation remains volatile, particularly as United recently slumped into the Premier League relegation zone following Nottingham Forest's recent success. While a dramatic 3-2 victory over Roma in the Champions League provided a temporary reprieve and a boost to squad morale, the domestic form remains a major concern for the fans. Ornstein added: "With the result mid-week against Roma, there was improved spirits, and let's see what happens against Villa today. The truth is there isn't a firm plan here at Old Trafford for what to do if they were to make a change". item.title: Ridle Baku called up to Germany squad
item.description: Ridle Baku called up to Germany squad Germany head coach Jürgen Klopp has given RBL defender Ridle Baku a late call-up ahead of the Nations League games against Serbia and the Netherlands . The 28-year-old joins teammate Brajan Gruda as the two RBL representatives in the 24-man squad. Klopp had praised Baku for his goal against Manchester City during the official squad announcement on Thursday, 5th November, and had mentioned that he was keeping the defender in mind as a replacement call-up. Baku has now been included in the squad following the news that Waldemar Anton would not be able to take part in the upcoming matches due to muscle problems. Aiming for his tenth Germany cap Baku will travel to the adidas Home Ground in Herzogenaurach with the team on Monday. The defender had been part of the squad in October for the Nations League matches against Serbia and Greece, but did not feature in either. Baku has been capped eight times at senior level for Germany, scoring twice in the process. So far this season, Baku has had a hand in four goals for RBL in 13 competitive games (3 goals, 1 assist) . item.description: MISSOULA, MONTANA - SEPTEMBER 14: Eli Gillman #10 of the Montana Grizzlies reacts after a second quarter touchdown against the Morehead State Eagles at Washington - Grizzly Stadium on September 14, 2024 in Missoula, Montana. (Photo by Tommy Martino/University of Montana/Getty Images) | Getty Images It’s evident that the pressure cooker that is November is heating up across the FCS. There was a different feeling of desperation in several games around the country over the past weekend and the results were that much more impactful. Week 10 brought with it upsets, bounce backs and thrillers that all helped lay shape to the playoff picture. Lehigh Dominates Colgate 33-7 for Key Patriot League Win Lehigh looked its old self again over the weekend. The Mountain Hawks made light work of visiting Colgate on Saturday afternoon. Still without starting quarterback Hayden Johnson, the Lehigh offense leaned on All-American running back Luke Yoder to get it done. Yoder ran for 181 yards and two touchdowns on 21 carries, pacing the ground game. Patrick Coan, playing in Johnson’s place, threw for 221 yards and a touchdown as well. The Mountain Hawks defense smothered the Raiders, sacking QB Jake Stearney twice and forcing him into two interceptions. When all was said and done, Colgate ran for just 77 yards and only had the ball for just over 20 minutes of game time. Now 6-1 in Patriot League play, Lehigh turns its attention to Richmond. Mercer Survives Chattanooga in OT The Bears kept their SoCon championship hopes alive on Saturday with a hard-fought 14-7 win over Chattanooga on the road. The low-scoring affair had to wait until overtime to get decided. The Mercer defense made a big fourth down stop but a missed 41-yard field goal attempt from kicker Simon Zeidan at the end of regulation sent the game to OT. On the first possession, Bears quarterback J.P. Pickles laced a seven-yard touchdown pass to senior receiver Brayden Smith on third down. Smith toe-tapped in the back of the end zone for his second TD of the afternoon. Three plays later, defensive lineman Ke’Vion Wellington hit Mocs signal caller Battle Alberson and forced a fumble. The defense jumped on it to seal the victory. Mercer got a big performance from that side of the ball which held Chattanooga to just eight first downs and forced three turnovers. The Bears now move to 8-2 overall (5-1 SoCon) as they get ready for a massive game against Tennessee Tech next week. Chattanooga falls to 6-4 (5-2 SoCon) and, in all likelihood, is out of the playoff chase. item.title: Superstitions prevail: If it ain’t broke, don’t move
item.description: As Erick Fedde and Kyle Teel celebrated the White Sox clinching the AL Wild Card series, fans could take a breath and relax following a day of superstitious rituals. | (Photo by Alex Slitz/Getty Images) I didn’t move. Not when Sam Antonacci doubled to open the second game of the American League Wild Card series against the Houston Astros. Not when Kyle Teel singled him home. And certainly not when Andrew Benintendi delivered a two-run single that helped the Chicago White Sox build a four-run lead before the Astros could record their second out. There I sat, practically frozen in place, convinced that the slightest movement might somehow bring Chicago’s offensive outburst to an abrupt end. Never mind that I was hundreds of miles from Daikin Park in Houston. Never mind that the White Sox players had absolutely no idea who I was, what I was wearing or whether I had gotten up to use the bathroom. And never mind that my position on the couch had precisely zero influence on a baseball traveling toward home plate at nearly 100 mph. The White Sox were scoring. I wasn’t moving. It wasn’t until Tristan Peters singled home Chicago’s fourth run and the inning finally ended that I allowed myself to get comfortable again. Welcome to the wonderfully irrational world of sports superstitions, where otherwise reasonable adults become convinced that a lucky jersey, a particular snack or the precise arrangement of living room furniture might determine whether their favorite team wins or loses. And apparently, I’m not alone. A little luck never hurt anyone My postseason wardrobe consisted of White Sox jerseys. Every game. No exceptions. When football season arrives, the situation becomes considerably more complicated. I pay attention to whether my team (either the Chicago Bears or Jacksonville Jaguars) is playing at home or on the road, choosing my jersey accordingly. I try to eat the same foods, snack at the same times and sit in the same location. It’s definitely easy for my wife. Honestly, she probably thinks it’s a little obnoxious. Sometimes a particular shirt becomes lucky. Other times, a hat gets blamed for a loss. I understand how ridiculous this sounds. I also know that if the White Sox had continued scoring every time I remained motionless during the playoffs, there’s a good chance someone would have needed to bring me dinner. But the impulse to create rituals around sporting events isn’t unusual. A 2018 study published in Sport Management Review examined how superstitions influence the experience of watching sports. Researchers found that these behaviors were associated with fans’ emotional states during games and that more superstitious fans were more likely to attribute outcomes to outside influences such as fate or officiating. In other words, fans aren’t necessarily trying to control a baseball game. They’re trying to control how helpless they feel while watching one. item.title: Previous Infantino ally Wenger considering FIFA presidency bid
item.description: FILE PHOTO - FIFA's Chief of Global Football Development Arsène Wenger stands in the stadium prior to the start of the UEFA Champions League final soccer match between Borussia Dortmund and Real Madrid at Wembley Stadium. (is associated with: «Previous Infantino ally Wenger considering FIFA presidency bid») Robert Michael/dpa Arsène Wenger is considering whether to put himself forward as a candidate for the FIFA presidency, the Press Association understands. The former Arsenal manager, 77, remains in the mix as one of a number of candidates UEFA could give its backing to as it seeks to put up a credible alternative to incumbent Gianni Infantino. However, Wenger is not yet seen as the preferred candidate, with others still being evaluated as well. It is understood he is still undecided over whether to run. Wenger’s reputation within football and close knowledge of the FIFA administration would make him a formidable opponent for Infantino if he did choose to go for it, with the Frenchman having served as FIFA’s chief of global football development since 2019. UEFA is expected to hold meetings of its executive committee as well as gather together its member national associations this coming week to hold further discussions on who should get Europe’s support. Infantino’s position appeared under threat when his plans to sell a minority stake in a World Cup company, FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE), to private investors came to light. The plan was rejected by three continental confederations, including UEFA, and even though Infantino later abandoned it, the European body said it had “lost confidence” in the Swiss and has since been working to identify someone to run against him. Wenger spoke out about the FFE plan on August 4, saying he was “not involved” in it and first became aware of it through media reports. He added: “The decision to withdraw the project was absolutely necessary and beyond question, because I firmly believe in an independent FIFA that serves our game with commitment, transparency, and integrity.” Kozo Tashima, the honorary president of the Japanese Football Association (JFA), announced on Thursday he would run for the presidency. Infantino has recovered and has rallied support from Africa, Asia, Oceania and South America. On Friday, he also received the backing of the member nations of the Caribbean Football Union (CFU). The election for the next FIFA president will take place at the FIFA Congress in Rabat, Morocco on March 18 next year.

item.title: Georgia reacts to after stomping Ole Miss football
item.description: The Georgia Bulldogs took it on the road this week to take on the Ole Miss Rebels and the Bulldogs had one thing on their minds and that was to win. Well, they did just that in a very big way. Georgia went into Oxford and dominated the Rebels by a 42-7 score. One big takeaway is how the Bulldogs defense has played since coming back from their bye week. They have flat out shut down the last two opponents and holding both Florida and Ole Miss under 10 points. Georgia's defense played lights out for the second week in a row and being able to do that against a game changing quarterback like Trinidad Chambliss is simply impressive. The Georgia offense took their game a couple of notches up and they didn't hold back against the Rebels. The Bulldogs racked up 481 total yards of offense against Ole Miss. Georgia rushed for 295 yards on 48 carries. Through the air, the Bulldogs passed for 186. Talan Taylor had four receptions, 140 yards and 3 touchdowns. Bulldogs running back Nate Frazier had over 100 rushing on the night. Georgia reacts to win over Ole Miss Kirby Smart reacts to Bulldogs' defensive staff "I'm really proud of the whole defensive staff. Glenn (Schumann) does a great job...Our kids stuck to the plan. The plan was to possess the ball offensively, own the line of scrimmage, we did that in the first half and stay aggressive on defense." Smart stated. The defensive staff did a tremendous job in back-to-back weeks when it comes to putting their defensive players in the best position possible to be successful. Because of the preparation from the Georgia defensive staff, Georgia's defensive unit caused havoc all night in Oxford. Gunner Stockton reacts to fast offensive start "It's a good feeling getting momentum early. We just try to stay on schedule and execute the plan...having that momentum makes a big difference." Gunner said. The Bulldogs did not let up and made an all-around statement to the country on how good they can be when they execute at a high level in all facets of the game. The Bulldogs will turn the page and look to continue it's momentum against the Missouri Tigers next week in Athens. Time may reveal whether that was a wise move for the Ohio State head coach, or it might be too late to know what would’ve happened if Day made a different move for the Buckeyes. But one way or the other, it appears to show the belief Day has in Fahey, whether well-founded or not. Fahey is a three-star true freshman from California, but it’s Fahey who Ohio State turned to when Julian Sayin got hurt at Indiana. The first-year college QB technically hung on to beat the Hoosiers, although he didn’t do anything at the tail end of that game. Fahey then lost at USC on Halloween and fell at home to Oregon on Saturday, a crushing third defeat for the Buckeyes that likely will ensure they miss the College Football Playoff. Day never put a different QB in the game even for a single snap. But there have been plenty of calls for Day’s firing, or for a QB change, or simply to try and figure out what happened to St. Clair. The reality is that Fahey hasn’t looked like a quarterback capable of leading Ohio State to great things. One quote by Day after Saturday’s game really said it all.
